correctness.rationale: The explicit two-band nilpotent partial isometry gives μ(E)=aI+ε(zE V+conj(zE)V*) and the commutator norm exactly 2ε² |Im(zE conj(zF))|. Disjoint three-color events have zE+zF+zC=0. Folding onto complete circle periods gives each moment cap r(s)=sin(πs)/π by the bathtub principle. For maximum mass w≥1/2, the two smaller colors can be disjoint arcs with perpendicular moments, achieving r(u)r(v). For w<1/2, cap moment lengths form an acute triangle and the PSD Gram determinant supporting plane has all positive coefficients, so its maximal oriented area is πr(a)r(b)r(c), attained by consecutive arcs. Both branches agree at w=1/2; strict log-sine concavity yields the unique maximizing density triple (1/3,1/3,1/3), global norm 3√3 ε²/(4π²).
residual_risks: Geometric rigidity is only asserted for periodic event partitions; ultrafilter positivity/limits follow from bounded WOT and finite additivity, not finite numerical tests.
